title: Deadline-driven admission controller and staged fallback profiles for reranker
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint is a high-value but latency-sensitive tier. During load spikes or regional degradation we currently either time out requests (causing client errors) or fall back to broad availability models without a controlled, SLO-aware degradation. This causes variable tail latency, customer-facing errors, and unpredictable cost.

Goal: Implement a deadline-driven admission controller plus a small set of staged fallback profiles so that every rerank request is handled with an explicit time budget and graded degradation strategy. Requests should either complete within the budget at the configured quality tier, or be deterministically degraded (shorter rerank depth, cached embeddings, cheaper model variant) rather than fail catastrophically. The feature must support per-customer SLO overrides and region-aware routing/fallbacks.

Approach:
- Add request-time-budget header (X-Rerank-Deadline-ms) and server-side deadline enforcement. The admission controller will allocate a time slice for each stage (embed fetch, candidate scoring, final sort) and enforce soft preemption when a stage would exceed its slice.
- Implement 3 staged fallback profiles (gold/silver/bronze):
  * gold: full rerank (full model + deep re-ranking), best-effort KV cache hit attempts, p99 target <= 200ms in healthy region
  * silver: reduced candidate depth + quantized model variant, allow partial cached candidate substitute, p99 target <= 350ms
  * bronze: cached re-ranks or vector-similarity-only fallback (no cross-attention reranker), p99 target <= 500ms and guaranteed success instead of error
- Admission controller will be SLO-aware: evaluate current regional queue length, recent p95/p99 latencies, and configured circuit-breaker state to decide admission (accept / enqueue / reject->fallback).
- Circuit breakers: two thresholds per region and per-tier: latency degradation and error rate. On trip, automatically shift new requests to next fallback tier and send alert.
- Routing: prefer local region; if local capacity is degraded (circuit breaker open) route to configured secondary region, applying region-specific fallback profile mapping.
- Observability: add per-request metadata to tracing (applied profile, time budget, admission decision, preempted stage) and dashboard with per-region SLO burn and fallback counts.

Trade-offs & rationale:
- Deterministic degradation (staged profiles) is preferable to opaque failures for product UX and billing predictability.
- Time-slicing increases code complexity but allows graceful partial results rather than all-or-nothing.
- We accept slightly higher steady-state cost for silver/bronze to avoid errors for high-value customers.

Open questions:
- Exact time slice split between embedding fetch and rerank stages for long context workloads. Proposal: dynamic split based on candidate set size with sane defaults (30% embed, 65% scoring, 5% buffer).
- How aggressive should regional failover be vs. chasing local capacity? See acceptance criteria for guardrails.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Add X-Rerank-Deadline-ms header support; server enforces deadline and emits metrics (accepted, preempted, fallback-used).; 2) Implement gold/silver/bronze profiles with configuration flags per-customer and per-route.; 3) Circuit breaker per-region with automatic profile shift on open and rollback after recovery.; 4) Regional routing policy that will route to secondary region when local circuit breaker open and preserve deadline semantics.; 5) Integration tests that simulate spikes and verify that customer-facing HTTP 200s are returned with degraded-quality responses instead of 5xx errors for bronze; 6) Dashboard showing fallback rate, per-region p95/p99, and SLO burn; 7) Canary rollout steps and rollback knob documented in runbook.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Triage meeting notes: high priority for several enterprise customers who saw 5xx during last incident. Agreed to pursue time-budgeting + staged fallbacks rather than adding more retries.

2025-02-20 - Arjun Patel: Architecture spike complete. Prototype admission controller implemented as a thin layer in front of reranker service; exposes admit(envelope) -> {accept|degrade_profile|enqueue|reject}. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-admission-proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-admission-proto/pull/6
2025-02-24 - Design review (Laura Kim): Request for explicit UI flags in Console to let customers pick fallback aggressiveness per-route. Added product ticket PM-4128 to track Console integration.
2025-02-26 - Ops (Samir Gupta): Defined circuit-breaker thresholds: trip when p95 latency > 3x baseline for 5m OR error rate > 2% for 3m. Will refine after canary metrics.

2025-02-27 - Arjun Patel: Integration test created that simulates embedding store latency; silver profile reduced candidate depth from 50->20 and switched to 8-bit quantized model, reducing mean latency by ~2.8x in the spike scenario. Test run dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/rerank/ENG-21137/spike-sim-2025-02-27
2025-03-01 - Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed changes; no customer data exfiltration vectors found. Recommend adding KMS-tagged logs for requests using cached results. See PR notes on instrumentation.

2025-03-03 - QA (Elena Park): Smoke tests green for gold/silver; bronze path returns cached fallback records and preserves schema. Found edge-case where very short deadlines (<=25ms) caused immediate bronze fallback; added graceful minimum threshold (>=50ms) to avoid client-level flakiness.

2025-03-04 - Arjun Patel: Preparing canary rollout in us-west-2 for low-volume customers. Canary plan: 2% of traffic -> monitor fallback rate, p95/p99, and error rate for 48h; rollback on >5% increase in errors or >25% increase in p99. Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/1984
Follow-ups: add per-customer override API, expand fallback profiles for on-prem deployments, and automate threshold tuning using historical traces (future work).
